City Through the Lens: Tokyo, Japan

Local videographers reveal how they film their hometown — the real locations, permit hurdles, and techniques you won't find in guidebooks.

🎬 Local videographer interview coming soon — subscribe on YouTube to see it first

Quick Takeaways for Filmmakers

  • Best filming season: Humid summers (35°C), mild winters
  • Top 3 landmarks: Shibuya Crossing, Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa), Tsukiji Outer Market
  • Main airport: Narita
  • Drone rules: banned in Tokyo wards without permit. Tripods OK in most public spaces.
  • Featured camera: Sony A7 IV

3 Must-Film Locations in Tokyo

1. Shibuya Crossing

Filming Tip: Shoot from Starbucks 2nd floor at dusk; handheld only, tripods blocked.

2. Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa)

Filming Tip: Golden hour 5-6 PM; incense smoke adds atmosphere; no flash indoors.

3. Tsukiji Outer Market

Filming Tip: Arrive 5 AM for tuna auctions; ask vendors before filming; tight spaces = wide lens.

Weather Reality Check

Humid summers (35°C), mild winters. Best Mar-May (sakura) and Oct-Nov.

Pro tip: Plan your shoot dates around these conditions. The "best" months mean better light, fewer crowds, and more predictable weather windows.

Airport Transfer & Arrival Tips

Narita (NRT) 60min Express or Haneda (HND) 30min monorail.

Factor in transfer time when booking flights. Arriving early gives you buffer for gear checks and acclimatization before shooting.

Permits, Rules & Local Etiquette

Drones banned in Tokyo wards without permit. Tripods OK in most public spaces.

Remember: Always ask before filming people, especially in religious or residential areas. Respect local customs — it's the difference between getting great footage and being asked to delete it.
